hits.text: OpenAI is letting two outside AI safety groups, METR and Apollo Research, look inside its model training. Apollo is placing six evaluators at OpenAI for four months to test for alignment faking and run its own safety tests; METR gets access to the training setup and can test whether OpenAI's systems interfere with evaluation. The evaluators cannot publish findings, but can push OpenAI to add safeguards or delay or withdraw a model, and Anthropic offers similar embedded access, though OpenAI's deal with Apollo is unusually deep and its commitment to publishing results is novel.

outsiders.text: Quoting his own Nov 13 article on building an AI agent swarm: Lauren Tan, an engineer on GrokBot at SpaceXSI, showed her coding setup at the AI Engineer Code Summit, where every agent mistake becomes a lint rule instead of a prompt, agents verify their own work with videos, screenshots and tests, and 3,000 PRs reached production in a month, with agents now merging most of their own PRs.

outsiders.draft_en: A coding agent should not need a better prompt. It needs a better rule. At the AI Engineer Code Summit, a GrokBot engineer showed her setup: every slip an agent makes becomes a lint rule, and 3,000 PRs a month reach production. Agents check their own work with video, screenshots and tests, and most of those PRs now get merged by agents themselves. If you are about to automate your codebase, watch how her agent swarm runs it first.

You can call it through the API on QwenCloud now, and smaller Qwen4 models get open weights soon.

This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
